page: Vultr voc-m-1c-8gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC processor with 1 vCPU consisting of 1 physical core and 1 thread. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is provided by a 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2896.39, placing it in the top 25% of tested instances. However, due to the single-core limitation, multi-core performance is weak. Memory bandwidth is relatively low, with read-only large block bandwidth at 22.42 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 20.94 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while database and Redis SET operations fall into the lower performance tiers.

This instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources combined with a relatively high memory allocation per core. The dedicated CPU allocation avoids the performance variability of shared-core instances. It is suitable for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, small-scale caching, and memory-sensitive utility workloads that do not require high multi-threaded compute or intensive memory bandwidth.
